# PixelForge

> An MIT-licensed, zero-dependency pixel art and sprite animation toolkit for AI agents and game developers. Compile editable JSON recipes to PNG sprite sheets, APNG animations, texture atlases, CSS and a Canvas player through a CLI or local stdio MCP server.

Requires Node.js 20 or newer. No build step, dependency installation, API key or hosted service is needed. Clone https://github.com/skulitom/PixelForge.git and run commands from the checkout. The package name is pixelforge-agent; the CLI command is pixelforge. Installation instructions use the GitHub checkout.

## Start here

- [README and setup](https://github.com/skulitom/PixelForge/blob/main/README.md): Quick start, CLI commands, MCP configuration, JavaScript API and exports.
- [Pixel art skill](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/skills/pixel-art/SKILL.md): A reusable workflow for authoring, inspecting and revising artwork.
- [Authoring reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/docs/agent-guide.md): Recipe fields, operations, frame inheritance, layers, inspection and resource limits.
- [JSON Schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/schema.json): Machine-readable recipe structure; the renderer also validates references and resource limits.
- [Art workflow and sidecars](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/docs/art-workflow.md): Quality checkpoints, native/silhouette/grayscale/onion inspection, regional edits, overlays, poses, scenes, PNG interchange and material passes.
- [Original quality lab](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/docs/art-quality-lab.md): Editable before/after study, candid self-review and remaining artistic limits.

## Workflow

CLI: node bin/pixelforge.js validate <recipe.json>, then node bin/pixelforge.js inspect <recipe.json> --grid, then node bin/pixelforge.js render <recipe.json> --out <fresh-directory>. Add --out <new-file.png> to inspect for a contact sheet image. For targeted edits, node bin/pixelforge.js patch <recipe.json> --changes <changes.json> previews every changed pixel; add --out <new-recipe.json> to save. Read JSON from stdin by replacing a filename with -. Results are JSON; errors go to stderr with exit code 1. Inspect every frame visually before final export.

MCP: run node /absolute/path/to/PixelForge/bin/pixelforge.js mcp --out /absolute/path/to/output [--root /absolute/path/to/project]. Transport is newline-delimited stdio; requests are limited to 16 MiB and an oversized line gets a JSON-RPC error while the server keeps running. Tools: pixel_help (guide, schema, example; topic poses, scenes, autotile or fx for sidecar schemas), pixel_validate (check a recipe; reports clipping locations), pixel_inspect (contact sheet and optional palette-key grids), pixel_patch (targeted set/insert/remove/paint edits, proposed cleanup of doubled corners and stray pixels, or a saved overlay, with a changed-pixel report and before/after image), pixel_render (export bundle and all-frame contact sheet preview; optional animation previews playback order; listFiles returns every file), pixel_compile (pose source, autotile template or pixelforge-fx particle source to a recipe revision), pixel_scene (render or export a scene manifest; assets may be revisions) and pixel_import (native PNG as base64 or a file inside the root to a lossless recipe revision). Validate, inspect, patch and render take { "project": <recipe> } or { "revision": <id> } from an earlier response, so a recipe is sent once. Palette and scene asset file references resolve only inside --root (default: the working directory). These recipe tools save immutable snapshots under the output directory's .revisions folder. Revisions survive restarts using the same output directory, and older rendered ids can be recovered from bundle recipes. MCP rendering creates a unique output folder per call.

Canvas corrections: add { "paint": "frames[blink]", "value": [{ "x": 9, "y": 7, "color": "k" }] } to patch changes. Painting updates final frame.pixels overrides in canvas coordinates after all layers, retaining editable operations. Palette names and hex set exact RGBA; transparent erases. Corrections propagate to inherited frames and appear in the comparison report.

Preserve editable source recipes. Existing CLI outputs are protected unless --force is explicitly selected. Coordinates are integer pixels; all exports are deterministic. The preview studio (node bin/pixelforge.js preview [recipe.json] [--open] [--port N]) listens on loopback only, on port 4747 or a free one when that is in use. Lossless non-interlaced 8-bit RGB/RGBA PNG import is supported. GIF export for sharing: node bin/pixelforge.js gif <recipe.json> --out <new.gif> [--animation name] [--scale 1-16] [--background color], or MCP pixel_render with "gif": {} (optional scale and background), which writes every animation to gifs/. Colours are exact and never quantized (a frame needing more than 256 is refused); alpha below 50% becomes transparent unless a background blends it; timing uses 10 ms steps; the result's notes report what changed. Pixel text: the text operation ({ "op": "text", "x", "y", "text", "color", "align"?: left|center|right, "spacing"?, "lineHeight"?, scale/flip/rotate }) draws a built-in font: printable ASCII, western European accented letters (À–ÿ, Œ œ Š š Ž ž Ÿ) and common symbols (€ £ © — … “ ” „ « »), with capitals 7 px, a line 8 rows, accents of capitals 2 rows above y, about 6 px per character, tabular digits and \n for lines; a character the font lacks is an error naming it. Frames for video editors: node bin/pixelforge.js sequence <recipe|source|scene.json> --out <new folder> --fps <24|25|29.97|30|60|n/d> [--size 720p|1080p|1440p|4k|vertical|square|WxH] [--scale 1-256] [--fit contain|cover] [--align top-left..bottom-right] [--offset x,y] [--background color] [--animation name] [--loops n | --seconds s] [--step n], or MCP pixel_render / pixel_scene with "sequence": { "fps": 30, "size": "1080p" }. It writes one PNG per video frame with straight alpha (whole-number enlargement, never resampled), sequence.json and a README with the ffmpeg command for a ProRes 4444 .mov; PixelForge itself encodes no video. Each video frame shows the pose active when it starts; NTSC rates are exact fractions; notes report poses that changed length or are never shown and whether the loop closes on the frame grid. fit cover takes the smallest enlargement that covers the canvas and crops the rest (placement.visible is the source rectangle left in view). Scenes render as shots; a scene that does not fill the canvas gets margins in its own background colour. The studio's Frames button downloads the same files as one ZIP and shows the equivalent command and MCP argument. Image generation models, GIF import, automatic quantization and native Aseprite files are outside the current scope.

Quality review: inspect supports --view color|silhouette|grayscale|onion|tile (3x3 repeat with seam evidence), --native, --diagnostics, --layers, --reference and --max-cells. MCP uses view/native/diagnostics/layers/reference/maxCells. pixel_render samples oversized previews explicitly without shortening exported animations. Regional patch verbs: grid (dots preserve, explicit erase clears), move and recolor, optional x/dot masks; scope frame preserves other poses with reported compensating corrections. The default is inherited propagation. Compile authored .poses.json files with compile (mirror poses, flipX parts, anchors and marker points exported as atlas pivots and points); compile a 2x3-tile terrain template into 47 blob or 16 cardinal tiles with autotile (each frame is one autotile operation naming its neighbour mask); inspect small rooms with preview room.scene.json, including autotiled tilemaps, and export them with scene. A scene placement with anchor: "frame" positions every frame by its own atlas anchor. Generated files use compact formatting (one line per record that fits in 120 columns, grids one row per line). Recipes can share a palette file ({ "$ref": "palette.json" }), override the palette per frame for palette cycling, remap stamp/copy colors, copy regions of symbols or earlier frames, add outlines (outside, inside or middle, with width and 3x3 direction masks for rim lights and drop shadows), dither with canvas-anchored Bayer or custom patterns and density ramps, apply seeded Markov-style rewrite rules (moss, cracks, cleanup), wrap frames for seamless tiles and pack trimmed atlases with sheet.trim. Diagnostics count doubled corners and stray pixels per frame; a cleanup patch change previews the fix. Pose sources rotate parts by any angle into editable symbols (RotSprite-style, no new colours) and tween eased in-betweens; scene trajectory keys take an ease. compile also turns a pixelforge-fx source (seeded emitters: burst or rate, angle, speed, gravity, drag, floor, sway, trails, dissolve, loops) into an ordinary recipe; an effect may take a timeline { length, rate or times, cues } in milliseconds instead of frames, where every named cue starts a frame, emitters can start or end at a cue by name, and a cue with at becomes a frame point in the atlas. Animations written as code: a .mjs draw loop exporting { name, width, height, palette, timeline, draw(ctx, t) } (plus optional colors, ramps, symbols, soft, pattern, units, snap) runs ordinary Canvas 2D code against a pixel-art context at every timeline frame; every command that reads a recipe also reads a loop (compile, validate, inspect, render, gif, sequence, preview). No anti-aliasing; one-pixel strokes without doubled corners; CSS colours must equal palette colours or be mapped in colors (unmapped ones are reported, never quantized); alpha, gradients and shadow blur dither solid keys, while keys on a ramp behave as light (lighter adds up, bands above a floor, fades cool), and a ramp marked surface: true (a wall, a floor) is raised along its own keys by light added onto it; drawImage takes symbols or { rows } and keeps their pixels (RotSprite turns); ctx.point(name, x, y) and cues with at become atlas points; ctx.layer(name) makes recipe layers; unsupported canvas calls are errors. Loops run as code locally through the CLI or compileLoop; MCP does not execute them. Sidecar formats have poses.schema.json, scene.schema.json, autotile.schema.json and fx.schema.json. Read the art workflow before using advanced formats.

## Complete recipes

- [Forest spirit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/examples/forest-spirit.json): Character animation.
- [Campfire](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/examples/ember.json): Animated effect.
- [Coin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/examples/coin.json): Collectible animation.
- [Shrine](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/examples/shrine.json): Dithered sky bands, a shading band, rim light, rewrite-grown moss and cracks, palette-cycled glow.
- [Caption](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/examples/caption.json): A lower third for video: pixel text typed in over an opening panel, timed in whole frames at 30 and 60 fps.
- [Sword swing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/examples/swing.poses.json): One part rotated through an eased, tweened swing (compiled: examples/swing.json).
- [Particle effects](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/examples/effects.fx.json): Sparks, looping embers, dust, leaves and shards (compiled: examples/effects.json).
- [Swinging lantern](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/examples/lantern.loop.mjs): A draw loop: an authored lantern swung by code, lighting a wall and floor through surface ramps with steps derived from the light (compiled: examples/lantern.json).
- [Slime hop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/skulitom/PixelForge/main/examples/slime.loop.mjs): A draw loop: squash and stretch, a dithered shadow, a landing cue and a feet point (compiled: examples/slime.json).
